entries.title: Psalms 106:1
segments: This psalm differs from

in being principally occupied with an enumeration of the sins of God's people.  It is supposed to refer especially to the Babylonish captivity, when the hope of speedy restoration had begun to animate the people.

entries.title: Psalms 106:3
segments: Whatever may be the state of the wicked, it will be well with those who fear the Lord and delight themselves in his commandments.

entries.title: Psalms 106:8
segments:
His name's sake; the display of his perfections. 
 
God deals with his people not according to their deserts, but according to the greatness of his mercy in Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Psalms 106:9
segments: The depths; the depths of the sea.

entries.title: Psalms 106:11
segments: In the end men will return, and see the difference between the righteous and the wicked; between him that serveth God, and him that serveth him not.

entries.title: Psalms 106:13
segments: Waited not for his counsel; did not quietly wait for God to send them help in his own time and way; but when any trial came, as the want of water or food, were very impatient and rebellious

entries.title: Psalms 106:14
segments: Lusted; as when they desired flesh.

entries.title: Psalms 106:15
segments: What wicked men desire, God may give them in anger as well as in mercy; his gifts may be perverted or abused to bring leanness into the soul.

entries.title: Psalms 106:18
segments: A fire was kindled; see

entries.title: Psalms 106:20
segments:
Their glory; for Jehovah, their real glory, they substituted a calf, the Egyptian idol, a shame to all who worshipped. 
 
No absurdity, wickedness, or folly is so great that wicked men, when left to themselves, may not fall into it.

entries.title: Psalms 106:23
segments: Stood--in the breach; as a soldier stands in the breach to keep back the enemy.  See Moses' intercessory prayer to prevent the destruction of Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 106:24
segments: Despised the pleasant land; upon the return of the spies.

entries.title: Psalms 106:26
segments: The wickedness of men is the cause of their calamities, and God in this life punishes men less than their iniquities deserve.

entries.title: Psalms 106:28
segments:
Baal-peor; one of the idol-gods of Moab. 
 
  The dead; dead idols as opposed to the living God.  See the narrative,
, etc.

entries.title: Psalms 106:30
segments: Executed judgment; by slaying the transgressors,

entries.title: Psalms 106:33
segments: The most meek and patient of men may be provoked to feel, speak, and act wrong, so as to bring distress upon themselves and others.

entries.title: Psalms 106:37
segments: Devils; demons, "unclean spirits," such as the idols of the heathen represented.

entries.title: Psalms 106:39
segments: Men are prone to follow their own inventions, rather than the revealed will of God.

entries.title: Psalms 106:45
segments:
His covenant; which he made with Abraham, to give his posterity the land of Canaan. 
 
The covenant of God standeth sure, and though men may despise its blessings God remembers it, and in due time will fulfil all its promises.

entries.title: Psalms 106:48
segments:
Amen; so be it, or let it be.  This doxology marks the close of the fourth book into which the Psalms were anciently divided. 
 
All the hope of God's people is in him, and it is for his glory that their hope in his mercy and grace should not be disappointed.
